thread:
Mia Chen: FYI I'm putting up a short proposal for telemetry on latency-sensitive routes (/v1/generate). Goal: minimal steady-state telemetry to meet SLOs + tiny sampled full captures for debug/support. Need ops + privacy 👀
Samir Patel: Sounds sensible. can you share the suggested sampling numbers? also we should avoid creating a new quota that surprises customers.
Mia Chen: proposal draft: keep per-request headers + latency + token counts always. full req/res capture only at `full_capture_rate: 0.005` (0.5%) for /v1/generate. default redact_level: high (PII heuristics + fuzzy mask). inspect TTL: 1h.
Lee Gomez: 0.5% seems OK but exposing a console meter for "inspect budget" is critical. customers will hit it and ask why support can't see a trace. dashboard should show used/remaining sample tokens per-tenant.
Anya Rivera: +1 on the console meter. privacy notes: any full captures must pseudonymize user identifiers before storage. we cannot store raw emails/SSNs. also require an audit-log entry when a human unmasks for debug.
Zack Cole: runtime concern: synchronous capture can add tail latency. we should do non-blocking offload: write a compact fingerprint immediately, then async upload full payload to separate capture service. that keeps the main path fast.
Mia Chen: agreed — plan is to write a compact provenance record inline and stream the full blob to the capture queue. enqueue should be best-effort and backpressure-tolerant (drop/metrics).
Samir Patel: for support replay, we need a safe temporary unmask flow. idea: short-lived HMAC token (TTL 15m) that lets support fetch a redacted-plus-pseudonymized payload. store an audit entry with requester id + reason.
Anya Rivera: HMAC fetch flow ok, but make opt-in explicit per-tenant. legal holds can override TTL. must surface retention windows in console.
Emily Tran: small UX ask: in the console, label the toggle "Enable sampled inspect captures (cost applies)" and add a hover tooltip: "Small percent of requests captured; PII is redacted by default; support can request temporary unmask with approval". also add a link to billing usage for sampled tokens.
Lee Gomez: on quotas — sampled captures should consume a separate "inspect quota" so normal quota math isn't affected. otherwise customers will think their requests are being charged twice.
Zack Cole: implementation note: prefer a token-weight model: full capture = N tokens (approx based on payload size) deducted from inspect quota. that maps to cost and makes rate-limits straightforward.
Mia Chen: good. ops question: how do we expose current effective sampling rate (considering canaries, overrides, per-route exceptions) in the API/console?
Samir Patel: expose a per-route computed field: `effective_capture_rate` that folds in global default, tenant override, and runtime canary multiplier. show also the source (global|tenant|canary).
Anya Rivera: finally, compliance: require an admin-level role to enable temporary unmask and a separate "view audit logs" permission. otherwise too many eyes.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: telemetry-capture-service v2 -> canary on prod at 2026-03-22T02:00Z (automated message).
Mia Chen: thanks. next steps: I'll send an RFC w/ the config schema + console mock and a short runbook for support unmask requests. please DM me any red flags. :thumbsup:
Zack Cole: one more runtime nit — ensure sampling decision is deterministic per-request-id when possible (hash-based) to improve cacheability and reduce variance.
Emily Tran: adding copy edit request for tooltip: "Captured requests are redacted by default. To request a temporary unmask, contact Support; access is audited."
Samir Patel: ack. if no objections by EOD I'll merge the config and start the canary.
Mia Chen: no objections here. merging tomorrow unless anyone raises a blocker.
Anya Rivera: approved from privacy side, flagged a follow-up for retention policy alignment with legal.
